description: A continuous sequencer over a field of stars: a line sweeps the display, and each star it crosses fires a trigger and a pitch

params.text: Sets the speed of the sweeping line as two to the power of its setting, a quarter speed at -2 and four times at +2
Starts and stops the sweeping line
Sets the root note that the pitches are quantised to
Picks the scale the pitches are quantised to, among them the Messiaen modes of limited transposition and the seventh chords
Chooses whether a star's pitch comes from its radius, small stars sounding higher, or from its position across the display
Picks a constellation and lays its stars out in the display
Removes every star from the display
Sets which way the line travels: purple left to right, blue top to bottom, aqua right to left, red bottom to top, or those four in clockwise, counter-clockwise or random succession
Throws every star to a new position
Gives every star a new random radius
Shifts the pitch of that coloured sweep by up to five octaves either way

inputs.text: A trigger starts and stops the sweeping line
Adds to the SPEED knob, every 2V doubling the speed of the sweeping line
A trigger returns the sweeping line to the start
Sets the root note from a pitch voltage, twelve semitones to the volt, in place of the root note knob
A gate throws every star to a new position
A gate gives every star a new random radius

outputs.text: Fires a 10V pulse as the line crosses a star, one polyphonic channel per star
Carries the quantised pitch of each star the line crosses, one polyphonic channel per star

notes: click in the display to add a star and drag it to move it; dragging a star out of the display removes it
the sweeping line is stopped when the module is added, so nothing fires until the play button is pressed or a trigger arrives at its input.
menu: Polyphony channels — sets how many stars can sound at once, Monophonic or 1 to 16
